statements.text: The Prime Minister is set to tell President Zelenskyy that the Prime Minister has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military and fiscal packages to provide urgent support in the coming weeks, and that the UK will accelerate delivery of critical air defence missiles. The UK is delivering £45 million of surface-to-air missiles and is standing by plans to fully implement a maritime services ban on Russian LNG exports. The UK will accelerate deliveries of Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which it says have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones, and will accelerate £10 million of the £45 million package to meet Ukraine's most urgent winter requirements. The UK has already committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5000 LMMs to Ukraine over the next four years.

The Prime Minister told the House that an energy ceasefire, with both sides stopping their attacks, is the quickest way to get diesel back onto world markets without rewarding the aggressor. He welcomed President Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire, and said President Zelenskyy has assured him Ukraine would immediately implement it when a start date is confirmed.

The Prime Minister said the UK assesses the incident at RAF Fairford is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard. The UK will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks and will bring further sanctions to restrict the capacity of Iran and the IRGC to do harm.

The Prime Minister confirmed the UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. On the table are a trade deal on food and drink, progress on emissions trading and linking energy systems, a new youth experience scheme and deeper cooperation on immigration. The Prime Minister said the UK's chances of a deal will be enhanced by being open to discussing the relationship with the EU in the longer term, and that after securing a successful summit, a serious dialogue should be set up on the options.

The Prime Minister said a trade deal on food and drink would add the equivalent of over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040, with the potential to add significantly more. The agreement on the table would lift a burden that can reach £1,400 on a single shipment for farmers and food producers, and would end export health certificates that can cost up to £200 each time for small businesses. The proposed energy deal could cut wholesale energy costs in Northern Ireland by 20%.

The leaders underlined that Russia had no interest in peace, and discussed how the UK could accelerate defensive support to Ukraine ahead of the winter. The Prime Minister said the UK would continue to develop innovative military solutions for use on the battlefield in Ukraine, including retrofitting British capability onto equipment gifted from other partners, and would continue its diplomatic efforts to support international supplies of defensive equipment.

A UK government spokesperson said Ukraine has repeatedly demonstrated it is serious about peace, while Russia has repeatedly rejected full and partial ceasefires and continued attacks on Ukrainian civilians and energy. The spokesperson said Russia could end this war today.

A UK government spokesperson said the UK will continue working with international partners to ensure Ukraine has the military and financial support it needs, and will maintain pressure on Russia through what it called the toughest sanctions regime ever imposed by the UK. The spokesperson said the UK remains committed to supporting Ukraine for as long as it takes.

The Prime Minister confirmed Britain's decision to send air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia to provide air-to-air refuelling support, and said a Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions.
The Prime Minister condemned the appalling attacks on King Khalid International Airport and said the UK will continue to stand with Saudi Arabia against the Houthis.

The Prime Minister said that in Berlin he and Chancellor Merz agreed a new partnership to tackle Russian hybrid threats. He confirmed the UK's commitment to establish a new National Centre for Information Defence, as recommended by the Foreign Affairs Select Committee.

The Prime Minister said the UK will take up the G20 presidency in 2027 and place AI centre stage, capturing its opportunities while guarding against its risks, with the aim of agreeing a single set of global principles and standards on AI during the presidency year.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey will use meetings at the IMF in Bangkok to urge partners to fully implement an equivalent ban on Russian LNG, following the UK's lead. He urged partners to back the ban, like the UK has done, to curtail the war chest funding Putin.

The site of Great British Railways' headquarters at Becketwell in Derby has been unveiled. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029, and the HQ will accommodate up to 450 GBR staff. It is estimated to bring a £151 million boost to Derby's economy and hundreds of rail jobs. Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over the next four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship.

Andy Burnham said that for too long people have put up with a railway that often lets them down, and that when people are trying to get to work, see family or get home, they should be able to rely on their train turning up.

Heidi Alexander said the biggest shake-up to the railways in a generation is underway, and that Great British Railways will bring the railway together around one mission, better services for passengers, with Derby at the heart of its future.

Pat McFadden said the foundation apprenticeship will give young people the chance to explore career paths in the rail sector while earning, and that it forms part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities for young people to earn or learn.

Claire Ward called it fantastic news for Derby, said she was delighted Great British Railways will be based in Derby bringing hundreds of jobs, and said she was particularly pleased about the 600 apprenticeship places.

The King has appointed William James Baxter QPM DL as Lord-Lieutenant of County Tyrone, succeeding Sir Robert William Lowry Scott, who retired on 17 June 2026. Mr Baxter served in the RUC and PSNI from 1973 until 2003, including as District Commander in Omagh from 1997, which included the day of the Omagh bombing in 1998.

The Prime Minister will invite the Scottish Government to work with the UK Government through No10 North and the Scotland Office to develop a new model of regional empowerment for Scotland. Andy Burnham said he is making an offer to the Scottish Government and that through No10 North the UK is rewiring the state, and wants regions in Scotland to be fully part of this.

Douglas Alexander said devolution has done a great deal, but power was never supposed to stop at the doors of the Scottish Parliament. He called the Prime Minister's offer to the Scottish Government a genuine one, and said the Scotland Office is ready to roll up its sleeves to make it happen.

The Prime Minister said Scotland, the most devolved nation in the UK, is one of the most centralised nations in Europe. He said the UK government is already giving local leaders in England more power over transport, skills and investment, and wants the same opportunities for Scotland and Scottish regions.
The Prime Minister said the Scottish government has agreed this week to match the UK government's £10 million to create two defence technical excellence colleges, one in the east and one in the west.

The Prime Minister said the UK is looking at devolving innovation, enterprise and employability funding for Scotland's people and places. He made an offer of DWP devolution, a model of localised employment support for Scotland shaped by Holyrood. He said the National Economic Council will meet in a couple of weeks with the First Ministers of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, for the first time since he became Prime Minister, to put that offer on the table.

The Prime Minister said around one in six young people in Scotland are not in education, employment or training. He said the review led by Alan Milburn is challenging government to build a system based on the Easterhouse principle of names not numbers, built from the bottom up.

The Prime Minister said the Scottish government has announced a long-term programme for local government reform, but that things must move faster and do more, and that if the UK does not move now, Scotland could lose out.
